messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm trying to wire the new JS SDK into the sample app for edge workers and running into a mess with our dual build outputs. needs eyes.
kevin: what specifically? bundle failure or runtime import error?
sara: +1 — paste the error and package.json snippet
maya: runtime. in Deno Deploy / Cloudflare Workers the import fails with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')" which happens when the app pulls the CJS build accidentally.
jonah: hmm are you using conditional exports? sometimes bundlers pick the wrong entry if fields are missing
maya: here's our package.json exports block (redacted):

```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

maya: And we also have "main": "dist/cjs/index.cjs", "module": "dist/esm/index.mjs", "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
kevin: that looks ok at first glance. but some edge runtimes (and older bundlers) prefer "main" when resolving for certain tooling. Deno/Workers should use import entry but if someone imports the specific file path or a bundler rewrites, you can get mixed runtime artifacts
sara: also check that the esm build doesn't pull any conditional requires (eg a crypto shim) that still use require() under the hood. that will blow up in edge.
maya: good call — we ship a small auth helper that detects runtime and conditionally requires node-fetch for Node; in ESM build that code ends up as `require('node-fetch')` because babel transform kept it. oops.
jonah: classic. for dual-publish we need to ensure builds are pure ESM/NO-CJS shims in the esm path. ideally the esm build should error at build-time if commonjs require exists.
kevin: we should also check the types entrypoint. TS consumers import from the package and sometimes the compiler follows "types" but other toolchains follow "exports" -> "types" mapping. mismatch can cause IDEs to show wrong types for default vs named exports.
sara: suggestion: add an explicit "./types": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } export and make sure exports default to import for browsers/edge:

```
"exports": {
  "./types": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" },
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "browser": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  }
}
```

maya: will that stop bundlers from picking the cjs build for edge?
jonah: not guaranteed, but adding "browser" helps some bundlers (webpack/rollup) prefer the browser field. plus making the esm bundle strictly ESM (no require) reduces risk.
kevin: another short-term mitigation — change package.json "main" to point to esm build while we fix transforms. many folks using modern runtimes will then get safe entrypoint.
sara: caveat: changing main to esm can break CommonJS consumers that do `require('our-sdk')` if their loader expects CJS. love to avoid that without a major version bump.
maya: also noticed auth/retry behavior differs between the cjs and esm entrypoints — in CJS we still import the legacy retry wrapper that retries auth refresh, but in ESM we ship a newer fetch-based retry logic. So some tests pass locally but fail in edge where CJS was chosen.
kevin: ugh that explains the flaky integ test failures. parity problem. we need a single source-of-truth for auth logic and ensure both builds reference it identically.
jonah: actionable plan:
- normalize auth/retry code into a runtime-agnostic module (no node-only shims) and compile it into both bundles
- add a bundler lint step that scans ESM output for "require\(" occurrences
- add an exports map sanity test in ci that simulates resolution with node, webpack, and a worker-like resolver
- temporarily set main -> esm to reduce edge fallout until fixes land

sara: I'll prototype the require-scan script and add a failing CI job if ESM build contains require() or "module.exports". will open PR.
maya: thanks. also I'll add a troubleshooting note to the sample app docs: if you see runtime errors in edge, check that you're pulling the esm entry (import path, bundler config) and that no node-only transitive dep slipped in.
ci-bot: ci/publish-preview — generated artifact for PR #412: eslint-plugin/no-cjs-in-esm added (checks will run on push)
kevin: perfect. one more tiny thing — types: some consumers import types via `import type {Client} from 'our-sdk'` and TS sometimes resolves to the cjs d.ts if exports mapping is ambiguous. the explicit "./types" export will help but we should test with `tsc --traceResolution` in CI.
jonah: agreed. adding tsc resolution check to the matrix.
sara: PR incoming for lint + tests. Maya, can you collect a minimal repro so we can add as an automated regression test for the sample app?
maya: yes, I'll paste a tiny worker repro into the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
